## 0. How to read this (learner notes)

* **gm/ID method** (book 1.2 and 2.3, pp.26-100): pick a gm/ID (inversion level) and an L per role, read the current density ID/W from the table, then `W = ID / (ID/W)`. High gm/ID = more gain per current but larger W and slower; low gm/ID = small VDsat headroom penalty is bigger but matching and speed are better. VDsat is estimated as 2/(gm/ID) (eq. 2.34) and every device must keep VDS >= VDsat + 50 mV.
* **Mirror ratios are integers**: one NMOS unit finger (2.5 um x L 1.0, about 10.5 uA at gm/ID 7.5) and one PMOS unit finger (5.0 um, about 4.9 uA) are multiplied, so the ratio between tails, sinks and references is exact in layout (matched devices are one device with nf fingers, never m, PLAN_V2 C6).
* **Resistor-diode bias**: I_ref = (VDD - VGS)/Rb. All currents move with VDD, temperature and the resistor section; the gain A1 = (gm/ID)(Itp/2I3) VR is a ratio of the *same poly type* (book eq. 5.7), so most of the resistor spread cancels; the corner table below shows what is left.

## 1. Bias (resistor-diode, v0) and shared nets

Topology: `VDD - Msw (ENB) - Rb - MBN (diode, VBN)`; MBN also drives the NMOS tails/sinks. `MBS` (1:1 with MBN) pulls the reference current through the PMOS diode `MBP` (VBP) which drives the PMOS tail and the VB2 branch (`MB2P -> MB2 on Vf = I*Rf`, so VB2 = Vf + VGS5, a one-finger replica of the M5 cascode at a quarter of its current). Vref = 0.48 VDD from an EN-gated divider with an NMOS switch and a 2000 fF decoupling cap; `EN = 0` opens Msw and the divider switch and parks VBN, VB2 low and VBP high.

## 2. Stage 1: hybrid complementary input + dump devices (T1 decision D-002)

Pairs at gm/ID 16 (NMOS) and 15 (PMOS), moderate inversion: A1 = (gm/ID)(Itp/2 I3) VR, so gain comes without current; fT well above the 100 Mb/s need. L_p = 0.4 um is the shortest PMOS length on every corner table with Leff margin; L_n = 0.5 um keeps the L-offset penalty small. Dump twins are copies of the pair devices. Tails and sinks at gm/ID 7.5, L = 1 um: low VDsat headroom cost, matching and output resistance from L. The cascode M5 (gm/ID 13, L 0.5) sets the fold pole (book eq. 6.38). RL = VR/IRL with VR = 1.17 V at tt (the resistor-diode bias makes VR follow (VDD - VGS_b) x RL/Rb: -14 % at ss/125 C, +12 % at ff/-40 C, so the tt value is chosen for the slow corner gain). The fold-node voltage F = I_b2 x Rf is the cascode offset Vf of the T1 spike (0.46 V at tt); it is squeezed between M3 VDS >= VDsat + 50 mV at ss/125 C and the steered PMOS pair VSD at VIC = 0.05 V at ff/-40 C (the two resistor cross corners leave 50-70 mV on both sides).

## 3. Stage 2: hysteresis comparator (book 3.3, handoff 7.5)

NMOS pair with PMOS diode + cross-coupled loads; alpha = nf_cross/nf_diode (positive feedback, book 3.3). The pair has **source-degeneration resistors Rs = 0.92 kohm each** (ppolyf_u_1k, the same poly as RL and Rb): the input-referred hysteresis is V_H,in = V_H2/A1 and both numbers move with temperature and process (V_H2 ~ 1/(gm/ID) of the pair, A1 ~ gm/ID x VR), so a plain pair spreads V_H,in about 4:1 over the corners while the window is 3.1:1 (8-25 mV). With Rs the trip is partly the ratio-metric drop I_T2 x Rs, which follows (VDD - VGS_b) x Rs/Rb exactly like VR does and therefore cancels against A1. For each (nd, nc) candidate the script finds the Rs that gives V_H,in = 14 mV at tt (large-signal solve of the pair from the table with body effect, book Ex. 3.11 method) and then evaluates V_H,in at the five proxy corners with the T1 gain spread over VIC (1.27x); the candidate with the LARGEST alpha whose max/min ratio is <= 2.2 wins (faster regeneration; chosen: **5/7 = alpha 1.400**).

## 4. Stage 3 (current-mirror differential-to-single-ended) and output chain

The two stage-2 outputs drive PMOS gates directly (a PMOS with source at VDD and its gate near VDD - |VGS| is a mirror copy of the stage-2 load diode); the copy of side A is mirrored by an NMOS diode and subtracted from the copy of side B at node d3, which therefore swings rail to rail with no tail current (so the NMOS-input swing problem of a diff-pair converter, d3 never below ~1.7 V, is avoided). EN gates a NAND2; chain NAND2 - INV - INV - INV is non-inverting (EN = 0 gives OUT = 0). Digital-style widths (book 1.2: the method does not apply to inverters), taper FO <= 4.

## 7. Offset budget (finding C3; Pelgrom A_VT = 7.15 mV um NMOS, PMOS 6.66 x 1.17 (measured MC is 6-17 % worse), Leff = L - 0.15, Weff = W + 0.1)

`sigma_total^2 = sigma_1^2 + (sigma_2/A1_min)^2 + (sigma_VH/2)^2 + (sigma_3/(A1 A2))^2`; A1_min = 4.59 (all corners), A2 = 4 assumed.

| term | contribution (mV, 1 sigma) | detail |
|---|---|---|
| sigma_1 stage 1 (worst path) | 2.80 | PMOS path 2.80 = pair 1.52 + dump twin 1.52 + M3 sinks 1.63 + RL 0.5 % 0.76 (quadrature); NMOS path 2.58 = pair 1.75 + twin 1.75 + RL 0.73 |
| (sigma_2 / A1_min) | 1.47 | sigma_2 = 6.76 (pair 4.06, loads 5.40) |
| (sigma_VH / 2) | 1.20 | hysteresis spread 2.40 mV input-referred (alpha error from load VT mismatch) |
| (sigma_3 / (A1 A2)) | 0.57 | sigma_3 = 10.41 mV |
| **sigma_total** | **3.43** | target 5 mV; trip window 2 mV + 6 sigma + 17.5 + 3 = **43.1 mV** <= 95 mV |

Monte Carlo is the judge (TB3_off, N = 1000); the hand budget only places the design in the right region.

## 10. Limits of this report (read before trusting it)

* Look-up tables exist only for tt/27 C, ss/125 C, ff/-40 C (L on the grid); fs, sf and ss/-40 C are covered only by simulation (TB1, TB2 smoke at worst5).
* The VDS of every device is a design assumption (table column OP_POINT in the script); TB1 compares the real `.op` point and fails on > 10 % ID or gm/ID, > 30 mV VGS.
* The hysteresis is solved large-signal at tt and scaled with gm/ID elsewhere; the A1 spread over VIC (<= 1.27x) is the T1 measurement, not a prediction.
* Dump twins are budgeted as a full extra sigma (T1 open item 1): conservative.
* Not implemented in v0 (the flags exist in the netlist; setting them aborts the build): failsafe, on-die termination, extra gain stage, constant-gm bias.
* VDsat is 2/(gm/ID) (book eq. 2.34) except NMOS L = 1 um devices, where the T1 spike measured BSIM vdsat = 0.80-0.86 x that value (factor 0.86 used). The simulator check of this netlist is sim/t2_op (tt/ss/ff/fs/sf, VIC 0.05/1.2/2.35 V): see sim/t2_op/results/op_table.md.
